workspaces.label: Head Nurse
workspaces.description: Nursing duty roster (drag & drop nurses onto beds per shift), roll call, supply indents, leave approvals.

screens.title: Nursing duty roster
screens.purpose: Plan duties by shift: nurses onto wards, zones and beds (drag & drop).

tasks.summary: Roster entries for a date range (planner grid, a week by default)
Staff I may roster, with default shift and approved leave in the range
Roster one or many duties (all or nothing)
Change a duty (shift, date, place, beds, on-call, notes)
Cancel a duty (reason kept; never deleted)
Repeat a period (e.g. last week) from a later date
Week check: rest days per person, staff per day and shift
Duty swaps of the staff I roster (open ones by default)
Record a swap agreed on the ward (staff without a login)
Approve a duty swap
Reject a duty swap
Live bed matrix (counts per ward + optional bed list)
Departments

rules: Week grid: one row per shift pattern (GET /rosters/staff → shift_patterns), one column per day; drag staff from the left column onto a cell. Save with POST /rosters (all or nothing: on an error, highlight details.entry_index).
Grey out the days in each person's `leave`; ROSTER_CONFLICT means the person already works an overlapping shift (a night shift runs into the next morning).
Mark the public holidays (GET /rosters/staff → holidays): rostering on them is allowed, and rostered staff work as rostered.
Edit with PATCH (send row_version as expected_version), never delete: cancel with a reason.
Past days are read-only unless you are HR (ROSTER_DATE_CLOSED).

The hospital works every day: Sunday is a column like any other (usually with fewer staff), and each person gets their weekly rest day on a different day. Staff on a fixed schedule show their weekly day off (default_weekly_off_days) greyed; rostering them that day makes it a working day.
'Repeat last week' = POST /rosters/copy; show the `skipped` list with its reasons. Offer 'Repeat, moving everyone's days on' (rotate_days 1): rest days, and Sunday duty, then rotate week by week.

Week check panel (GET /rosters/week): NoRestDay in amber (each day beyond the allowance is paid as extra duty), NotRostered in grey; under the grid, a row of counts per day and shift from `days`, so a thin Sunday shows before the week starts.

Swaps tab: GET /rosters/swaps (Accepted = both colleagues agreed, waiting for you) → Approve, or Reject with a reason. For staff without a login, 'Record swap' (POST /rosters/swaps) when the two agreed in person. You never decide a swap you are part of (SWAP_SELF_APPROVAL). Duties taken over show their swap_id.
Keep the grid live with the roster.changed event, the swaps tab with roster.swap.updated.
Ward duties: pick the beds each nurse looks after (bed_ids); the nurse then sees them in 'My beds this shift'.

tasks.summary: Roll-call sheet: who is rostered today and who has arrived

rules: For wards and hospitals without a badge station: tick who is present at the start of the shift; staff who already scanned a badge show their first_in and cannot be ticked again.
Send each entry's own roster_date: after midnight the sheet still lists last night's running shift, which belongs to yesterday's date.
For a late arrival, or an earlier day's shift (HR only), send the actual arrival time (`at`); it must fall within the shift.

shared_screens.title: Report an incident
shared_screens.purpose: Anyone reports an incident, an adverse event or a near miss, the same day, without blame.

tasks.summary: What to report: the incident types
Report an incident, an adverse event or a near miss
The incident register
One incident
The list of sentinel events and how to report (PDF)
Find a staff member for a form (badge facts only)
Departments
Returning-patient lookup by name / phone / CNIC / UPMRN / MRN
Admissions (default: all live ones; admissions desk queue)
The death register
Formulary search with live stock colour
Live bed matrix (counts per ward + optional bed list)

rules: A button on every workspace's toolbar. Form: the type (GET /incident-types, grouped by area, sentinel types marked), incident or near miss, harm, when (now by default) and where (department, ward, place), who was affected (a patient: search by MRN; staff: GET /staff/lookup, any reporter may use it), what happened (facts, not blame) and what was done at once; 'Keep my name confidential' (reporter_confidential).
Medication errors: the stage and the medicine; theatre events: the operation and the phase (INCIDENT_DETAILS_REQUIRED). Send an Idempotency-Key: a double click must not report twice.
After sending: show the incident number and 'The Quality Officer will review it'. 'My reports' = GET /incidents?mine=true.
Link 'What to report' to GET /incidents/sentinel-list/pdf.

Patient fields by permission: offer the patient search (GET /patients/search), the admissions (GET /admissions), the operations (GET /ot/bookings), the death records (GET /deaths), the formulary (GET /drugs/search) and the wards (GET /beds/matrix?include_beds=false) only to a user holding a permission the call accepts (its x-permissions against GET /auth/me); anyone else describes the patient in the text.

tasks.summary: The incident register

The incident report with its analysis and actions (PDF)
Departments

Sign: INCIDENT_ANALYSIS_INCOMPLETE lists details.missing. A sentinel event needs at least one factor of the system, not only 'Individual' or 'Patient' (MSDS CQI 107: blame alone is not an analysis).

Departments

One action
Close an action: done with the evidence, or cancelled

shared_screens.title: Connect to server (first run / server unreachable)
shared_screens.purpose: Find the hospital server, trust its certificate once, remember its addresses. Full contract and Electron code: the 'Connecting terminals' guide.

tasks.summary: How terminals reach and trust this server — works before login
Identify this terminal (location + mapped printers) — works before login

rules: Order: policy registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Haspataal\Terminal > %ProgramData%\Haspataal Terminal\terminal.json > the saved choice > this screen.
This screen: broadcast a LAN discovery request (UDP 47632) and list the servers found; also allow typing an address (https://SERVER-NAME).
Before trusting a server the first time, show its CA fingerprint and require IT to confirm it matches the Control Center (skip the question only when a provisioned fingerprint matches).
Pin the hospital CA; never accept a server whose CA fingerprint differs from the trusted one (show 'This is not your hospital server').
After connecting, call GET /meta/server-info and store ALL urls as alternates; if the one in use fails during a shift, try the others before showing 'Server unreachable'.
While unreachable: keep the current screen and unsaved input, show a banner, retry with back-off (1, 2, 5, 10, 30 s), resume the WebSocket with resume_from when back.

shared_screens.title: Login
shared_screens.purpose: First screen on every terminal: username/password, LAN diagnostics, terminal identity overlay.

tasks.summary: Log in (returns tokens, profile, roles, workspaces)
Identify this terminal (location + mapped printers) — works before login
Change own password
The server's license state: show a banner when it needs attention — works before login
Is the server there? (unauthenticated, no database)
Server health (unauthenticated; used by the login screen)

rules: Before showing the form, ping GET /health/live every 5 s; if it fails show 'LAN / server unreachable' (cable, Wi-Fi, server) instead of hanging. When it answers, GET /health says whether the server is degraded (HTTP 503, its database down: 'The server is starting or has a problem: ask IT'), in maintenance, or licensed (license.state).

In maintenance (GET /health maintenance_mode) show maintenance_message word for word: it is the text IT wrote in the Control Center (e.g. 'Back at 02:30'), never replace it with one of your own; keep polling until maintenance_mode is false.

License banner: GET /meta/license on this screen (and data.license after login, the system.license event, every 10 min). state grace = persistent banner with message, days_left and the vendor contact on EVERY screen, work continues; state locked = only the Super Admin can log in, others get LICENSE_INVALID at login and token refresh (show message + details.vendor).
Show the terminal MAC/IP overlay (Ctrl+Shift+I or an info icon) from GET /terminals/whoami for IT support.

A Settings button (and Ctrl+,) opens the Settings window before login: GET /settings/sections without a token answers signed_in false and the This terminal tier only (connection and LAN diagnostics, this terminal's location and printers, the login screen's language and zoom). It writes nothing on the server.
If user.must_change_password is true, force the change-password form before anything else (other endpoints answer PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED).
ACCOUNT_LOCKED / RATE_LIMITED: show error.message and error.retry_after_seconds; never retry automatically.
Store the refresh token with Electron safeStorage; keep the access token in memory only.

shared_screens.title: Workspace launcher
shared_screens.purpose: Multi-role users pick a workspace; single-workspace users skip this screen.

tasks.summary: Workspaces the user may open (multi-role launch screen)
Current user, roles, permissions, workspaces, preferences
The establishment's profile and services, with the configuration revision

rules: If exactly one workspace: open it directly.

My Workspace (self_service; every_employee true in GET /auth/workspaces, roles usually []) is every employee's, listed after the role workspaces. Open it like any workspace (its window sends X-Active-Workspace: self_service), but do not count it for the launcher: a user with one role workspace opens that one directly and reaches My Workspace from the user's menu, a multi-role user also from the launcher. A guest login (the PHC inspector) has no My Workspace.
Allow opening several workspaces in separate windows at once.

Every request of a workspace window sends X-Active-Workspace: <its code> (one of GET /auth/workspaces; another answers WORKSPACE_NOT_ALLOWED): the audit trail records the window, and F1 help defaults to it. The launcher sends none. It never changes what the user may do.
Hide menu items whose x-permissions the user lacks (permissions are in /auth/me).

One build of the frontend serves every profile (Clinic, II C, II B, II A, I) and every change of it: nothing is downloaded or switched by a flag. Read GET /establishment after login and again on establishment.changed, then list each workspace as views.workspaces says (hidden: not listed; records: marked Records; open_work: with the banner) and each screen as views.screens says; a workspace or screen it does not list is core and always shown (to the users with its permissions). Inside a screen hide an operation of x-capability-gates (or only the choice its `when` names) while its service is not in `active` (the server refuses it anyway: CAPABILITY_INACTIVE). What is shown follows the services, never the profile's category: the category picks the inspection framework, the letterhead and the few rules a screen names (the clinic's complete consultation).

shared_screens.title: Settings (avatar or Ctrl+,)
shared_screens.purpose: One Settings window in every workspace: my preferences and password; the facility's profile, services and policy settings; IT's users, hardware and emergency actions: each tier only for the users it belongs to.

tasks.summary: The Settings window: the tiers and sections this caller may open (also before login)
My preferences (theme, language, UI scale, PDF download)
Update my preferences (only the fields you send)
Change my password (same as /auth/change-password)
Request a control-setting or privileged-access change (applied at once for an Owner)

rules: Theme: Light / DarkHighContrast.
Language en/ur is per USER (loaded at login), not per machine; bundle Noto Nastaliq Urdu; no bilingual labels in grids.
UI scale slider (100–250 %) and Ctrl +/- drive the SAME Electron zoom factor; persist via PUT /settings/me.
'Documents' section: 'Download a set of documents (the PHC inspection pack) as: separate PDFs, one per click (default) / one combined PDF' → pdf_download Separate | Combined. Never offer a ZIP.

Open it from the avatar menu or Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on macOS) in every workspace; build its navigation from GET /settings/sections, never from role names: the facility tier opens facility_profile and the policy settings, the system tier opens the IT console's parts.
Policy settings marked is_control show 'Owner approval': for anyone but an Owner, Save sends POST /admin/change-requests and the row shows 'Waiting for an Owner' until approval.resolved.

Before login the same window opens from the login screen with the This terminal tier only (signed_in false): Server connection and LAN diagnostics (GET /health, GET /meta/server-info: the addresses and the CA fingerprint, GET /meta/license), This terminal (GET /terminals/whoami: location, printers, cash node, the MAC sent as X-Terminal-Mac), and the login screen's language and zoom, kept on this terminal until a user logs in (then GET /settings/me decides). After login the tier stays, last.

shared_screens.title: Help: the end-user handbook
shared_screens.purpose: The searchable, role-filtered handbook of the software for the hospital's staff, shipped inside the app: how to use each screen they may use, step by step, in English and Urdu, so the hospital needs no software training.

tasks.summary: The end-user handbook's outline for the logged-in employee (only what they may use)
My preferences (theme, language, UI scale, PDF download)

rules: Build the handbook as the developer guide 'The end-user handbook' (get_guide('end-user-handbook')) says: one page per screen (screens/<screen id>) and one per workspace (workspaces/<code>), written for the hospital's staff (where to click, what happens, what the system refuses and why, what to do on each error message), in English and Urdu (the user's language preference, GET /settings/me), with screenshots of YOUR UI.

RBAC is the server's: GET /meta/handbook after login (and after a role change) returns the pages this user may read; show only those pages in the help window and in its search index; a page whose screen is not in the answer is never shown, linked or searchable for this user.

Localhost-only searchable site: the pages are a static site generated at the app's build (MkDocs-style with a client-side search index), bundled in the app and served to the help window from an HTTP server bound to 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port (or a custom app:// protocol); never on the LAN, never on the hospital server. Works offline. Print-friendly for the training room.

Entry points: 'Help' in the avatar menu (opens the user's handbook home: their workspaces and a search box) and a '?' button on every screen (opens screens/<id>). The home lists the user's own workspaces first (yours true).
Keep it current: the page ids are the screen ids of the catalogue; what_changed in the MCP server lists screens added or changed since the last build, so the pages are revised with the UI.
In a workspace window, call GET /meta/handbook?workspace=<that workspace>; never show another workspace's pages in that window.

You never approve your own request (SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN): self_decision forbidden shows 'Awaiting another approver'; allowed_with_note (the Owner of a solo practice, solo_practice_mode in GET /meta/settings) asks for the note, and the answer comes back solo_self_approved.

shared_screens.title: PHC inspection interview practice
shared_screens.purpose: Every member of staff rehearses the questions the PHC's surveyors may ask them, with answers that quote the hospital's own settings and records, a few minutes a day.
shared_screens.workflow: PHC inspection interviews (the vendor's request of 2026-10-08)

tasks.summary: My practice deck: the question of the day and what to rehearse now
One question: other ways of asking, the model answer with the hospital's facts, key points, follow-ups, pitfalls, what to show
Record how well I knew a question (Knew, Partly, DidNotKnow)
My readiness: questions known, chapter by chapter, my streak and my last mock interview
The PHC inspection interview questions (filter by role, chapter, indicator, type, words)
The roles and how many inspection interview questions each rehearses
A role's pocket guide: questions, key points and model answers (PDF)
A role's pocket guide as a print payload, in English or Urdu
Mock interviews, newest first (staff who do not conduct them see their own)
One mock interview: each answer and the actions it raised

rules: Login card (every workspace, msds.interview.practice): `question_of_the_day` from GET .../my-deck with a 'Practise' button; hide it when null.

Flashcard: show the question (and, on 'Ask it differently', one of `variants`); the user answers aloud or in their head; 'Show the answer' reveals `model_answer`, then the `key_points` as a checklist; three buttons Knew / Partly / Didn't know → POST .../rehearsals; then the next card of `due`. Show `follow_ups` as 'The surveyor may ask next', `pitfalls` as 'Avoid', `show_me` as 'Be ready to show'.

The aim is that staff can explain what they actually do, as the hospital's SOPs say: never present the model answer as a script to memorise. Show under every answer: 'If a key point is not true on your ward, tell your in-charge: it is a gap to fix, not a line to learn.' (the answer's `notice`, in its language)
Facts: values from the hospital's settings are already filled in `model_answer`; a fact with `set` false shows as a bracketed prompt: never invent a value.
Badges: the PHC type (Mandatory red, Operational yellow, always with its word), the indicator number in the hospital's category (`indicators_in_category`), 'Adapted to our SOP' when `adapted`.
Progress (GET .../my-progress): ready %, the streak, per chapter knew / partly / not known / not rehearsed; the last mock interview with its score (open it: GET .../mock-interviews/{id}).

Browse all (GET .../questions?mine=true, then any role) and 'Print my pocket guide': in English GET .../pocket-guide/pdf (a PDF: one click, one file); in Urdu GET .../pocket-guide?lang=ur, laid out by the app right to left and printed from the terminal (the server's PDFs are Latin script only).
INTERVIEW_QUESTION_NOT_APPLICABLE: the hospital took the question out; drop the card and refresh the deck.

Language (the vendor's request of 2026-10-09): send `lang` (en or ur) or rely on the user's preference (PUT /settings/me language); every answer says its `lang`, so offer an English / اردو switch on every card. Urdu (`direction` rtl): lay the texts out right to left in Noto Nastaliq Urdu (bundled in the app); medicine names, test names and the hospital's own records inside stay in English as typed. `text_status` Draft: show 'Draft translation' beside the answer until the vendor's native-speaker review; `question_en` gives the English wording a surveyor may use.

shared_screens.title: Mock PHC interviews
shared_screens.purpose: A supervisor questions a member of staff as the PHC's surveyor would, records each answer and turns the gaps in practice into corrective actions.
shared_screens.workflow: PHC inspection interviews (the vendor's request of 2026-10-08)

tasks.summary: The staff to question in a mock interview (with or without a login)
The questions to put in a mock interview: the member of staff's weak points first
Record a mock PHC interview: each answer Met, PartlyMet or NotMet, and the actions for the gaps
Mock interviews, newest first (staff who do not conduct them see their own)
One mock interview: each answer and the actions it raised
The roles and how many inspection interview questions each rehearses
One question: other ways of asking, the model answer with the hospital's facts, key points, follow-ups, pitfalls, what to show
The action register (mine: the actions I own)
Departments

rules: Only for msds.interview.conduct. Pick the member of staff (GET .../staff; staff without a login are listed too, `is_me` greyed) and the role, then 'Plan' → GET .../mock-interviews/plan (count 6): the questions with their `reason`; the examiner may swap any for another of the role (GET .../questions?role=).

During the interview show the examiner one question at a time with its `key_points` (GET .../questions/{key}) and, hidden behind a toggle, the model answer; never show the answer to the person questioned.

Each answer: Met / PartlyMet / NotMet; a note is required unless Met (VALIDATION_ERROR). When the answer shows a gap in PRACTICE (the SOP is not followed, equipment is missing) offer 'Raise an action': type, description, owner (a user_id from GET .../staff), due date.

Save once at the end → POST .../mock-interviews with an Idempotency-Key; show the score and the actions (they appear in the action register, GET /quality/actions?source=MockInterview). MOCK_INTERVIEW_SELF: nobody examines themselves.
History: GET .../mock-interviews (filters: employee, role). Staff without conduct see only their own.
Language: the plan, the questions and the reasons come in the examiner's language (`lang`); ask in the language the member of staff works in, as the surveyors do.
